questions.q: What is the key difference between authentication and authorization?
options: Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you're allowed to do once you're in
They are two names for the exact same process
Authorization happens before authentication, never after
Authentication only applies to biometrics, authorization only applies to passwords
questions.explain: Authentication is proof of identity; authorization is the separate decision of what that identity may access or do.

questions.q: In Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), how do users get their permissions?
options: By being assigned to a role, which carries a fixed set of permissions
Each user negotiates their own unique permission set individually
Permissions are assigned randomly at login
Only the system administrator ever has any permissions
questions.explain: RBAC ties permissions to a role (like an AD group or Salesforce profile); users inherit access by role membership, which is why it scales well.

options: The resource's owner decides who gets access and can change that decision at any time
Access is decided entirely by a government classification system
Users are never allowed to share anything they own
It requires a central administrator to approve every single share
questions.explain: DAC puts access decisions in the hands of whoever owns the file or resource, as seen in NTFS permissions and Google Drive sharing.

questions.q: Why can't the owner of a classified document override Mandatory Access Control (MAC) rules?
options: MAC enforces fixed labels/clearance levels centrally, regardless of what any individual owner wants
MAC doesn't actually apply to documents, only to network traffic
Owners under MAC always have unlimited sharing rights
MAC is identical to DAC with a different name
questions.explain: MAC removes discretion from the owner entirely — access is enforced centrally by matching classification labels to clearance, as in government and military systems.

questions.q: Which real-world systems are most associated with RBAC specifically?
options: Active Directory security groups and Salesforce profiles/permission sets
Government military classification systems exclusively
Personal file sharing on a home computer with no accounts
SELinux mandatory labels exclusively
questions.explain: Active Directory groups and Salesforce profiles are classic real-world RBAC implementations used broadly in business software.
